For flat schemas, `controller_response_schema()` combines the descriptions into the `type` property's description at lines 357–360.

The descriptions are for the action variants, not every individual JSON field or every callable tool. Tool parameter descriptions come from each tool’s own schema/catalog entry; the controller prompt only describes how to choose and invoke tools in the `tool_calls` variant.

completion.continuation_response:
No—not every tool is individually described in the design spec.

- The runtime does require every `ToolDefinition` to have a non-empty `description` field (`tools/registry.py:16–20`), and the tool sources shown all provide one: built-ins such as `search_code`, `read_file`, `run_command`, and `query_graph`; PTY tools; sub-agent tools; team tools; memory/skill tools; web search/fetch; and planning tools.
- MCP tools are different: `mcp/client.py:187–192` uses the server-supplied description, falling back to `"<name> (MCP server '<server>')"` if absent.
- The spec’s §4.6.3 is selective, not a complete catalog. It explicitly details `write_todos`, `run_command`, and `dispatch_agents`, lists the “clean for children” tools (`search_code`, `read_file`, `list_directory`, `read_env_profile`, `search_semantic`, `query_graph`, `recall`, `read_skill`), and says `remember` and PTY tools are excluded; MCP descriptions are server-supplied third-party text (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-subagents-design.md:311–325`).

So the accurate answer is: **all exposed runtime tool definitions have descriptions, but the spec does not document every tool’s description; it documents the relevant policy and selected descriptions, with MCP descriptions delegated to the server.**
